doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Radio listening as youths
summary: Grimes listened from Dixieland to Parker and Miles, plus the Dorsey Brothers and Gene Krupa.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Was the radio part of learning music in those days for you guys?
The radio. I mean did you listen to music?

I used to listen to a lot of music from Dixieland up to about ’53 when you’d hear Charlie Parker and Miles Davis and those kind of groups. But in between I used to listen to the Dorsey Brothers you know, like, and, you know, all those associated players like Gene Krupa.
I wanted to play with some of them that I never did play with them.
